newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds rally in strong trade after NTMA auction.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds rally in strong trade after NTMA auction.

text.p: Irish bonds strengthened across the board in non-stop trade on Tuesday in the wake of a successful domestic auction and market-cheering CPI data from the U.S., dealers said.

"It's been a very solid day for Irish bonds," one dealer said. "The market, already in good shape, rallied on the back of the auction and received a further boost from the U.S. CPI numbers, which seem to have underpinned bond markets overall at a higher level."

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 74 pence from Monday's close at 102.25 to yield 5.82 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 1.05 Irish pounds from the close at 108.73 to yield 6.59 percent.
The National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said on Tuesday that a 150 million Irish pound auction of the eight percent bond due 2006 was covered 5.15 times.
The stock, sold to primary dealers in a competitive auction, achieved an average price of 108.24 to give an annual yield of 6.77 percent, the NTMA said.

Bond markets around the globe benefitted from softer than expected U.S. CPI data on Tuesday, with consumer prices rising just 0.1 percent in March versus a forecast rise of 0.2. U.S. Treasuries leapt after the news, leading all bond markets higher.
The figures helped cool concerns about the possibility of a near-term interest rate hike to rein in the U.S. economy.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 131 basis points over Germany in the five-year area and 84 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area.
"We're outperforming Germany by five basis points on the 10-year, and the five-year spread has narrowed by 12 basis points," a dealer said. "We've outperformed across the curve today."
Tuesday's auction attracted good international interest, he added.
